**DK50* Crohns sygdom** is a WHO-classified diagnosis code used within the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]] (DANIBD) to identify patients with Crohn's disease. It serves as one of the two primary diagnostic categories that form the foundation for quality measurement, clinical benchmarking, and epidemiological tracking in the Danish national registry for inflammatory bowel diseases.

According to the 2023 DANIBD annual report, which details quality data from October 1, 2022, to September 30, 2023, the prevalence of this specific diagnosis code among all IBD patients varied by region. The code accounted for 40% of all IBD patients in [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]], 45% in [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]], 41% in [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]], 43% in [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]], and 40% in [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] [^src1]. 

In the subsequent 2024 report, the DK50* code continued to be central to evaluating key quality indicators, including the use of biological and small-molecule drugs, surgical interventions, and patient characteristics [^src2]. By standardizing this coding, the registry supports cross-regional quality monitoring and the development of evidence-based treatment guidelines for IBD care in Denmark.
